rationales: 35°C is below the usual optimum temperature for human enzymes.
39°C is slightly above the usual optimum temperature for most human enzymes.
37°C is approximately normal body temperature and the optimum for many human enzymes.
41°C is above the usual optimum and may denature enzymes.
Stroma is the fluid inside a chloroplast, but chlorophyll is embedded in the thylakoid membranes.
Thylakoid membranes contain chlorophyll for capturing light energy.
The plasma membrane does not contain chlorophyll.
Cytoplasm does not contain chlorophyll in leaf cells.
The esophagus transports food and does not have villi.
The stomach does not have villi for nutrient absorption.
Villi are found in the small intestine, where they increase the absorptive surface area.
The large intestine does not have the nutrient-absorbing villi characteristic of the small intestine.
Platelets help form blood clots.
Erythrocytes carry oxygen and do not form clots.
Neutrophils are white blood cells that defend against infection.
Basophils are white blood cells involved in inflammatory responses.
4000–5000 is below the approximate textbook count of 7000 white blood cells per cubic millimeter.
5000–6000 is below the approximate textbook count.
6000–7000 does not include the commonly stated count range beginning at about 7000.
7000–8000 is the range that includes the approximate textbook count of 7000 white blood cells per cubic millimeter.
Bu Ali Sena is chiefly known for his contributions to medicine and philosophy.
Abdul Malik Asmai studied animals in detail and is noted for zoological writings.
Jabir Bin Hayan is chiefly associated with chemistry.
Al-Razi is chiefly known for medicine and other scientific work.
Starch is a large polysaccharide and therefore a macromolecule.
Proteins are macromolecules.
Lipids are generally treated as macromolecules in this context.
Water is a small molecule and is an example of a micromolecule.
An observation is a recorded fact, not a tentative explanation.
A theory is a well-supported explanatory framework, not a tentative initial explanation.
A hypothesis is a tentative explanation of an observation.
A deduction is a conclusion logically drawn from premises or a hypothesis.
Ernst Haeckel proposed the third kingdom, Protista.
Édouard Chatton distinguished prokaryotes from eukaryotes but did not propose Protista as the third kingdom.
Margulis is associated with later revisions to classification, not the original proposal of Protista as a third kingdom.
Schwartz is not credited with proposing Protista as the third kingdom.
NADH is produced during glycolysis but is not one of the two 3-carbon breakdown products.
FADH₂ is not produced as a direct product of glycolysis.
Glycolysis splits one 6-carbon glucose molecule into two 3-carbon pyruvic acid molecules.
Acetyl-CoA is formed later from pyruvic acid during aerobic respiration.
Chromatin is DNA and associated proteins, not the main site of ribosomal RNA formation.
Cytoplasm contains ribosomes but is not where their RNA is formed.
Mitochondria have their own genetic material and ribosomes but are not the main site of cellular rRNA formation.
The nucleolus is the main site of ribosomal RNA synthesis and ribosome-subunit assembly.
Protein synthesis is carried out by ribosomes.
Mitochondria are the main sites of cellular respiration and ATP production.
Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, not mitochondria.
Lipid storage is not the mitochondrion's primary function.
During G1, the cell grows and makes enzymes and other materials needed for DNA replication.
G2 occurs after DNA replication and prepares the cell for division.
DNA duplication takes place during S phase, rather than the preparatory enzyme production described here.
M phase is when the cell divides.
Most enzymes are not carbohydrates.
Most enzymes are not lipids.
Enzymes are generally proteins.
Enzymes are generally not nucleic acids, although some RNA molecules can act as catalysts.
Phosphorus is a component of ATP, nucleic acids, and many coenzymes.
Iron is not a general structural component of ATP, nucleic acids, and coenzymes.
Iodine is not a component of ATP, nucleic acids, and coenzymes.
Boron is not a component of ATP, nucleic acids, and coenzymes.
